Key Themes 2027

US Key Themes 2027

Our highest-conviction call for 2027 is that economic growth will be comfortably above the consensus.

The US economy heads into 2027 after absorbing an energy price shock, a hawkish shift from the Federal Reserve, and a change of control in Congress. We expect GDP growth to strengthen to 2.5% from 2.4% in 2026, well above the consensus forecast of 2.1%. That resilience masks an economy that’s reliant on a single engine.

Four themes will shape how 2027 unfolds; together, they describe an expansion that’s strong but one where risks are building. We doubt those vulnerabilities will cause major problems in 2027, but they’ll determine how painful the next downturn proves to be.

Theme 1: The AI buildout has more room to run. We expect the non-AI economy to rebound in 2027, but reliance on continued strength in AI isn’t going anywhere. Growth is broadening across industries, while households’ high exposure to AI stocks will support consumer spending.

Theme 2: Inflation will remain sticky. Repeated shocks and bottlenecks, along with a solid underlying economy, mean core inflation will remain above the consensus in 2027.

Theme 3: Fiscal policy mostly adds noise, but it could fuel growth and inflation. Divided government will bring bruising fights over shutdowns and the debt limit, while doing little to curb tariff, immigration, and geopolitical uncertainty. A deficit-financed bipartisan deal could lift defense and healthcare spending ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

Theme 4: The seeds of the next recession are being sown during a strong expansion. A debt-financed surge in investment, weak hiring by small businesses, and a postponed labor-market adjustment to AI mean we expect the next downturn, when it arrives, to be more painful, with less cushion from fiscal policy.
